# Monitoring Checker Schema

The Apify actor [`apify/monitoring-checker-schema`](https://apify.com/apify/monitoring-checker-schema) as typed Telo kinds, generated from its build **0.0.194**. The module's version is that build number, and every run it starts is pinned to exactly that build, so the input types below are the ones the actor really runs with.

The monitoring checker schema is a part of the Apify Monitoring Suite (apify/monitoring). See its readme for more information and how to use this.

## Pricing

Free — you pay only for the Apify platform usage (compute units) of the run.

Runs are charged to the Apify account whose token the `ApifyClient` holds. See the [Store page](https://apify.com/apify/monitoring-checker-schema) for current prices.

## Import

```yaml
imports:
  Actor: oci://ghcr.io/telorun/apify/apify-monitoring-checker-schema@0.0.194#sha256-…
```

Pin the digest with `telo upgrade`. The module re-exports `ApifyClient`, so it is the only import needed.

## Usage

```yaml
kind: Actor.ApifyClient
metadata: { name: apify }
token: !cel "secrets.apifyToken"
---
kind: Actor.Run          # or Actor.Start for runs longer than 5 minutes
metadata: { name: scrape }
client: !ref apify
maxTotalChargeUsd: 1     # optional: timeout, memory, maxItems, maxTotalChargeUsd
---
kind: Run.Sequence
metadata: { name: main }
steps:
  - name: scrape
    invoke: !ref scrape
    inputs:
      options: "…"
```

- **`Run`** calls Apify's synchronous endpoint and returns `{ items }`. Apify holds the request open for at most 300 seconds; a longer run fails with HTTP 408.
- **`Start`** starts the run, long-polls it until it finishes, and returns `{ run, items }`. A run that ends `FAILED`, `TIMED-OUT` or `ABORTED` raises `APIFY_RUN_NOT_SUCCEEDED` with the run as `data`.

## Input

Only these fields are accepted — `telo check` rejects any other.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `options` | string | yes |  | Validation options — List of validation options selected by list of dataset IDs or by the regular expression. It is possible to define minimum item count, maximum item count and validation schema (type-check) for each defined validation options. |
| `subjectType` | string | yes | `"ACTOR"` | Subject type — Type of the resource to checked. |
| `name` | string | yes |  | Subject name — Name of actor, task or dataset to be checked. |
| `id` | string | yes |  | Subject id — Id of actor, task or dataset to be checked. |
| `runs` | array |  | `[]` | List of runs — List of specific actor or task runs. |

## Output

The actor publishes no dataset schema, so `items` are untyped objects.
